rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide an algorithmic device (software using nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to recommend rents or occupancy) to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use one to set rental rates or occupancy levels. Each month and each property of use is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Tenants may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees to the prevailing party; City may enforce with civil and criminal remedies.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 11, §§98.1101-98.1104 (O-21955 N.S.)

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego and to persons who sell or license algorithmic devices to them.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes software that only publishes aggregated historical data over 90 days old or public data, affordable-housing program rent tools, and appraisal software.

rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
